title: kbgit.py sorts commits into content and code lanes
goal: _tools/kblane.py classifies paths and commits: a path is content when it is under a kb root (kb/<name>/** for a name not starting with _), under kb/_querylog/, a backlog item (kb/_self/backlog/*.json), _tools/aliases.csv or _tools/lint_baseline.txt, and code otherwise; a commit is code when any path it changes against its first parent is code. kbgit.py lane [A..B | REV] prints each commit's short hash, its lane and the code paths that decided it (default @{upstream}..HEAD, as check-trailers). Every path ql_deliver.auto_kinds accepts and every kbgit.MECHANICAL path is content; kblane.py imports neither kbgit nor backlog; tests.py -k TestLanes covers each boundary with planted commits

gates.question: Which paths are the content lane (direct push)? Everything else is the code lane (merge request).
options: kb roots, kb/_querylog, kb/_self/backlog items, _tools/aliases.csv and _tools/lint_baseline.txt (process docs in kb/_self/*.md go with the code they describe)
the same plus kb/_self/*.md process docs
kb roots only; backlog items and query-log data go through merge requests too
gates.recommendation: kb roots, kb/_querylog, kb/_self/backlog items, _tools/aliases.csv and _tools/lint_baseline.txt (process docs in kb/_self/*.md go with the code they describe)

notes: Content is what the autonomous writers write (ql_deliver.auto_kinds: the query-log store, root articles and ledgers, kb/<root>/_retrieval data, _tools/aliases.csv, the bug item of a revert) plus what kbgit.py fix rewrites after a rebase (kbgit.MECHANICAL, which holds _tools/lint_baseline.txt), so a sync that rebases content never turns into code. The classifier is its own module so ST-3i3dl6xg “kbgit.py is a CLI over kg_* modules” moves only CLI wiring; kbgit.py, backlog.py and the CI job import it.
